To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two point mutations within the −232/−232 to +85 tox promoter/operator and two missense mutations within the dtxR gene were found to correlate with the level of the toxin synthesis by C. diphtheariae strains isolated in the Republic of Belarus.

the nucleotide substitution at position −184 in the tox promoter/operator and two missense mutations A147V and I214L in the C-terminal domain of the Dtxr protein were associated with the high-level of toxin production.
the level of toxin expression by Corynebacteria is determined by the nucleotide sequence in the tox promoter/operator and the amino acid sequence in the C-terminal domain of the DtxRx repressor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of point mutations in the tox promoter/operator and the dtxR gene associated with the high level of the toxin synthesis by toxigenic C. diphtheiae strains.
the identification of point mutations associated with the level and the regulation of the toxin production in C. diphtheiae strains.
a new mechanism that may contribute to the high level of the toxin expression by C. diphthieriae strains isolated in the Eastern Europe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mutations in the tox promoter/operator and in the C-terminal part of the Dtx R gene are associated with high-level production of diphtheria toxins by C. diphtheariae.
the mutations in the tox promoter/operator and DtxR gene are not the main cause of high level of toxin production.
the mutations in the promoter/operator region of the tox and the dtxR gene were associated with the level and the pattern of the toxin production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of the toxin produced by the toxigenic C. diphtheiae strains is determined by two factors: (a) mutations within the tox promoter/operator; and (b) mutations in the dtxR gene.
the level of the toxin synthesis in C. diphtheariae is regulated by the tox promoter/operator region, the dtxR gene, and the DtxR repressor protein.
the tox promoter/operator mutations and the dtxR gene missense mutations are responsible for the enhanced level of toxin production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
point mutations within the tox promoter/operator and the dtxR gene can lead to increased toxin production and, consequently, to the emergence of highly toxigenic strains of C.  diphtheriae.
the tox promoter and dtxR gene may be involved in the regulation of the toxin production in C. diphthieriae strains.
the level of the toxin synthesis in C. diphtherea is controlled not only by the tox promoter/operator region but also by the dtxR gene.
